draft.summary: October adds up: the opening balance of $2,549.00 plus $4,175.00 in, minus $2,355.25 out, gives a closing balance of $4,368.75. Adding $630.00 of completed rows after the month gives $4,998.75, which matches the account balance recorded on Nov 3. Every budget line is within its approved amount; Fundraising costs has the least left, at $51.25. Nothing was left open at month end. All 7 payments count as approved by two officers only because the demo data holds no signatures. There is one exception. The Oct 24 car wash logged 87 cars at $15.00, so $1,305.00 was expected, but only $15.00 was received. The records show no trace of the other $1,290.00.

points.check: Ask the car wash volunteers and the Treasurer how the car wash money was collected and where the rest of it is now, since the records show only one PayPal payment.
points.basis: Car wash, Oct 24: 87 cars logged at $15.00 = $1,305.00 expected; $15.00 received; $1,290.00 has no record.

points.check: Confirm with the Treasurer that each of the 7 payments was in fact approved by two officers, because the records hold no signatures to show it.
points.basis: Two keys: 7 of 7 payments counted as approved because the demo data holds no signatures.

points.check: Ask the Treasurer what the completed rows dated after the month are, since they are needed to match the Nov 3 account balance.
points.basis: Closing balance $4,368.75 plus $630.00 of completed rows after the month = $4,998.75, matching the Nov 3 account balance.

points.check: Mention to the Treasurer that the Fundraising costs line is nearly used up before any further fundraising spending for the season.
points.basis: Fundraising costs: $948.75 paid of $1,000.00 approved; $51.25 left.
